# Copilot Instructions — minimega

See `AGENTS.md` at the repo root for project overview, structure, build/test/check/install
commands, and common pitfalls — this file focuses on conventions specific to
reviewing and generating changes.

## Language-Specific Conventions (Go)

- Format with `gofmt` (tabs, standard Go style). `scripts/check.bash` fails
  the build if `gofmt -d -l` reports diffs on `cmd/`, `internal/`, `pkg/`.
- Run `go vet` clean — also enforced by `scripts/check.bash`.
- Preserve the existing copyright header style at the top of the file being
  edited (Sandia/NTESS). Copy the header format from a neighboring file in
  the same package rather than inventing a new one.
- Dependencies are vendored under `vendor/` with `GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor` (set
  in `scripts/env.bash`). If you add/bump a dependency in `go.mod`, run
  `go mod vendor` and commit the resulting `vendor/` changes.
- `go.mod` has several `replace` directives pointing at
  `packages/github.com/...` — these are in-repo forks of third-party
  modules. Patch the fork under `packages/`, not the upstream module.
- Never hand-edit `internal/version/version.go` — every build/test/check
  script regenerates it from `VERSION` + the current git revision.

## Python Bindings

- `lib/minimega.py` is generated by `pyapigen` during `scripts/build.bash`
  (from the built `minimega` binary) — don't hand-edit it; change the CLI
  handler definitions in `cmd/minimega/*_cli.go` instead and regenerate.
- `lib/setup.py` packages the bindings for PyPI (see
  `.github/workflows/python-publish.yml`).

## Framework Patterns — minicli CLI framework

- All minimega/minirouter commands are declared as `minicli.Handler` structs
  (see `pkg/minicli/handler.go`) grouped into `var xCLIHandlers = []minicli.Handler{...}`
  slices, one per `cmd/minimega/<name>_cli.go` file.
- Handler slices are wired into the running CLI via `registerHandlers("x", xCLIHandlers)`
  calls inside `cliSetup()` in `cmd/minimega/cli.go`. A new handler slice
  that isn't registered there will compile but never be reachable — check
  this first if a "missing command" bug is reported.
- `HelpShort`/`HelpLong` strings on handlers are the source of truth for
  generated docs (see Maintenance Matrix below) — keep them accurate and in
  the existing Markdown-ish style used by neighboring handlers.

## Test Conventions

- Unit tests: standard Go `_test.go` files, run via `go test` or
  `./scripts/test.bash` (iterates `cmd/`, `internal/`, `pkg/`).
- End-to-end tests: `tests/<name>` (a minimega script or `.mm` file) paired
  with `tests/<name>.want` (expected output). When you add or change
  observable CLI/VM behavior, add or update the matching `.want` file in
  the same change — a behavior change without an updated `.want` file will
  fail the e2e comparison.
- Full VM/container e2e tests require Linux + QEMU/KVM + Open vSwitch +
  dnsmasq; they are not expected to run in a plain sandbox.

## Code Style Notes

- `.editorconfig` at the repo root governs whitespace per file type: Go
  files use tabs; Python uses 4-space indent (88-col soft limit); YAML/JSON
  use 2-space indent. Respect it even if your editor doesn't auto-apply it.
- Commit messages and PR/branch names follow
  [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/)
  (`type/description` branch names, `type(scope): subject` commits) — see
  `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`. Recent upstream history (e.g. `fix:`, `feat:`,
  `chore:` prefixes) confirms this is actively enforced in review.

## Maintenance Matrix

Use this table to know what else to touch when you change something:

| If you change... | Also update... |
|---|---|
| A CLI handler's `HelpShort`/`HelpLong` or command pattern in `cmd/minimega/*_cli.go` | Nothing by hand — docs regenerate via `scripts/doc.bash` (`apigen`) into `doc/content/articles/*.article`. Do add/adjust the relevant `tests/<name>` + `tests/<name>.want` if behavior changed. |
| A new `*_cli.go` handler slice | Register it in `cliSetup()` in `cmd/minimega/cli.go` (`registerHandlers("<name>", <name>CLIHandlers)`), and confirm it's covered by one of the `-sections` passed to `apigen` in `scripts/doc.bash` if it should appear in generated docs. |
| `go.mod` / `go.sum` (new or bumped dependency) | Run `go mod vendor` and commit the `vendor/` diff. If it's a patched fork under `packages/github.com/...`, update the `replace` directive instead of pulling upstream. |
| `VERSION` | Nothing else — `internal/version/version.go` is regenerated automatically at build time from `VERSION` + git revision. |
| Anything under `cmd/`, `internal/`, `pkg/`, `docker/`, `lib/`, `packaging/`, `scripts/`, `web/` | Check `CODEOWNERS` — these directories have explicit owners who should review the PR. |
| The set of runtime/build dependencies (QEMU, OVS, dnsmasq, etc.) | `.github/workflows/build.yml`'s `apt-get install` list, and the `docker/Dockerfile` / `docker/docker-compose.yml` if the container image needs them too. |
| Python binding behavior | `lib/minimega.py` is generated — change the underlying CLI handlers instead, and verify `scripts/build.bash`'s `pyapigen` step still produces valid output. |
| CLI/API surface intended for the public docs site | Confirm `scripts/doc.bash`'s `apigen -sections` list still covers the new/changed commands. |
